title: Conor Oberst Solo Tour Visiting Cave, Haunted Hotel
excerpt: Conor Oberst is taking the long way around America in 2027.
content:
Conor Oberst is taking the long way around America in 2027. The Bright Eyes frontman has announced An Alleged Evening With Conor Oberst, a 49-date solo tour that will wind through theaters, ballrooms, historic spaces, an underground cave and, for its final two nights, the famously haunted Stanley Hotel in Estes Park, Co. The trek marks Oberst's first solo headlining tour since 2019 and promises extended evenings drawing from across his vast catalog.

The itinerary is as characteristically offbeat as the billing. Among the more distinctive stops are the Caverns, an underground performance venue in rural Pelham, Tn.; the Henry Miller Memorial Library in Big Sur; San Francisco's Castro Theatre; Cine El Rey in McAllen, Tx.; and La Rosa, a converted Benedictine monastery chapel in Tucson, Az.

More from Spin:

The tour closes May 14-15 at the Stanley Hotel, the Colorado landmark that inspired Stephen King's The Shining and once hosted magician Harry Houdini. Oberst has partnered with PLUS1 for the solo tour, with $1 from each ticket going to his Poison Oak Project. The organization supports equity for LGBTQ+ people, with a particular focus on the trans community. Tickets go on sale Friday (Nov. 13).

The announcement follows a busy stretch for for both Oberst and Bright Eyes. The latter wrapped a fall tour in its Omaha, Ne., hometown in late October, while Oberst made his filmmaking debut the prior month with Invention 13, a co-directed Super 16mm short starring Emory Cohen and featuring a voiceover from Phoebe Bridgers. The film's score was composed by Bright Eyes member Nate Walcott.

Bright Eyes will visit New York's Brooklyn Paramount in January for three performances celebrating the band's two landmark 2005 albums. The Jan. 11, 12 and 14 shows will feature I'm Wide Awake, It's Morning and Digital Ash in a Digital Urn performed in full; the first two dates are already sold out.
